purpose.p: How to write the layout of a Kajenn Press site: Python build code that produces one HTML document with slots for contents, reading site texts, assets and page data.

list.item: A websites installation with its render worker (the render extra).
A site open for editing; templates are added through template_add (REST, MCP, or Help me).

step.title: Write build code
step.p: A template is Python that defines build(source, data). It runs once in the render worker when the template is added; the result is stored as a plain Source Bag and replayed at every rendering. The engine is gramlot or htmlbuilder.
HTML attributes are keyword arguments; class is written class_, for is for_. The document has exactly one html root.

example.title: A minimal template with two slots
example.code: def build(source, data): doc = source.html(lang="en") head = doc.head() head.title("^page.title") head.link(rel="stylesheet", href="^assets.site.url") body = doc.body() body.div(node_label="hero", kpress_slot="hero") body.div(node_label="body", kpress_slot="body")

step.p: build reads nothing while building: values that change per page or per language are Data pointers, strings starting with ^, resolved at rendering.

step.title: Declare slots
step.p: An element with kpress_slot="name" is a slot: the place where a page shows the content assigned to it. kpress_slot=True names the slot by its label path. Slot names are unique in a template, and a slot is an element able to hold content (div, main, section, article, aside, header, footer, nav, td, li and similar).

A slot that also has kpress_iframe="URL" is filled by that iframe in the browser; the content assigned to it is the static fallback written in the page, which search engines and readers without JavaScript see.
Contents are filtered before they enter a slot: HTML through an allow-list of tags, attributes and URL schemes; Markdown is converted first. Scripts, styles and iframes inside a content are removed.

step.title: Read page data

table.title: Data pointers available to every template

row.cell: This page's path in a language, for a language selector.
A site text in the language being rendered; the main text where its translation is missing.
The address of an asset the page holds: a content-addressed path when published, a data: URL in previews.

step.p: Site texts are the template's own words: menu labels, menu links, footer sentences. They are set with site_text_set, translated like contents, and shared by every page.

example.title: Menu and language links from the example site
example.code:
NAV = ("overview", "features", "start") LANGUAGES = ("en", "it")
nav = inner.nav(id="site-nav", aria_label="Main navigation") for key in NAV: nav.a(f"^texts.nav_{key}", href=f"^texts.href_{key}") for code in LANGUAGES: nav.a(code.upper(), href=f"^page.urls.{code}", hreflang=code, class_="nav-language")

step.title: Leave the SEO to the page
step.p: The page's SEO is written into the head after the template: title, description, canonical, robots, Open Graph and Twitter tags, JSON-LD and hreflang links. Those tags written by the template are removed first, so a template may keep a title for previews without producing a duplicate. The lang of the html root is set to the language being rendered.

step.title: Data from connections
step.p: A page's Data may hold resolvers that read a named connection at rendering, such as a configuration value. The connection's address and credentials come from the server that renders, never from the page. A value enters the page as text, or as filtered HTML when the resolver says so.
A published page with resolvers is rendered again by the site server when its cache time expires (600 seconds by default), and kept in a local cache; a page without resolvers is served as published.

rule.why: Values that differ per page or language would be frozen at template time.

rules.rule: Read Data while building; use ^ pointers.

rule.why: Every language then gets its own menu and links.

rules.rule: Put the template's words and links in site texts.

limits.limit: Template code is trusted code: the render worker is a separate process, not an OS security sandbox.
A template is shared by every language of a site; there is no template per language.

facts.fact: plain_template runs build(source, data) once and stores the plain Source.
An unknown engine or a template that does not build is refused as invalid_input or invalid_template with diagnostics.
Slots come from kpress_slot; duplicate names and elements that cannot host content are refused.
Contents are filtered with an allow-list (nh3); Markdown is converted with markdown-it first.
Templates receive page.title, page.language, page.urls, texts and assets.
Template title, description, robots, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter and JSON-LD tags are replaced by the page's SEO.
Connection resolvers default to a 600-second cache time.
The example layout renders every example page in English and the home page in Italian.
